# mattpocock-skills-dsh
Matt Pocock's engineering and productivity agent skills, packaged as a plugin for the **DeepSeek Har
engineering and productivity agent skills, packaged as a plugin for the **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)**.
27 skills — grilling, spec and ticket flows, TDD, code review, domain modelling, and more — installe
d as one bundle. The skill bodies are **verbatim** from upstream `mattpocock/skills` v1.3.2. Only th
e packaging is new: a Cordis plugin that registers a skill provider on `ctx.skills`, so every agent
preset in a profile sees these skills.
The skills are "plug-and-play, not vibe coding": small, composable, and meant to be edited. Fork the
m and make them your own.

## What you get
27 skills. `model + user` means the agent may reach for the skill on its own; `user only` means it i
s invoked by you, because upstream marks those flows `disable-model-invocation: true` — a prescribed
sequence that should not fire by itself.
| Skill | Invocation | Description |
| `ask-matt` | user only | Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in

this repo. |
| `code-review` | model + user | Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch
, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding
standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both rev
iews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branc

h, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X". |
| `codebase-design` | model + user
| Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a modu
le's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or A

I-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary. |
| `diagnosing-bugs` | model +
user | Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/

"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow. |
| `domain-modeling` | model + use
r | Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or

editing a GLOSSARY.md, or recording or editing an ADR. |
| `grill-me` | user only | A relentless in

terview to sharpen a plan or design. |
| `grill-with-docs` | user only | A relentless interview to s

harpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go. |
| `grilling` | mod
el + user | Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to

stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases. |
| `handoff` | user only | Compact

the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up. |
| `implement` | us

er only | Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets. |
[该节后续省略]
## Layout
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The provider scans `skills/` one level deep, reads each `SKILL.md`'s YAML frontmatter for `name` and
`description`, and loads the body only when a skill is actually requested. Each skill advertises a
directory `resourceBase`, so a relative reference inside a body — tests.md, `scripts/hitl-loop.templ
ate.sh` — resolves for the reader.
## Upstream fidelity
Bodies are byte-for-byte upstream; nothing is translated or rewritten. Four deliberate packaging dif
e byte-for-byte upstream; nothing is translated or rewritten. Four deliberate packaging differences:
1. **Flat skill directories.** Upstream groups skills into `skills/engineering/…` and `skills/produc
tivity/…`. This package ships `skills/<name>/`, the layout the provider scans. `scripts/sync-skills.
mjs` performs the flattening from upstream's `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` skill list, so the promote

d set stays upstream's decision.
2. **No `agents/openai.yaml`.** Those files are hints for another h

arness. Every `SKILL.md` and every relative reference it names is shipped.
3. **Invocation mapping.*
* Upstream's `disable-model-invocation: true` becomes `invocation.modelInvocable: false`, so a user-

invoked flow stays user-invoked instead of becoming an auto-trigger.
4. **Rank 550.** Below the bund
led root's 600, so a harness-shipped skill of the same name always wins. A plugin must not shadow th
t's 600, so a harness-shipped skill of the same name always wins. A plugin must not shadow the host.
`retro`, `pr` and `implement-spec` are part of upstream's promoted set and are included; the unpromo
ted `in-progress/`, `misc/`, and `deprecated/` buckets are not.
## Verify
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The check loads `lib/index.js` through the export shape Cordis reads, replays the registry's own val
idation over every candidate and definition (name pattern, non-empty description, boolean invocation
flags, provider identity, finite rank, directory resource base), resolves every relative reference
each body names, and confirms `dsh.plugin.json`, `package.json`, and the provider agree on the skill
set. What it cannot prove is runtime presentation: the skill catalog a session sees, and the Plugin
Manager row, need a Harness restart to observe.
## Sync to a newer upstream
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then set `version` in both `package.json` and `dsh.plugin.json` to the upstream version, and update
`contributes.skills` if the promoted set changed. The check fails when the manifests and the provide
r disagree, so a missed edit cannot ship silently.
